_comment: SYNTHETIC canned reply of the plan-generation model for the worked-example prediction. Used by pipeline.test.ts and as the reference shape for plan.v1. Not a real model output.
proposition: Within two years of 2025-11-03 (i.e. by 2027-11-03), approvals for new data centers will be restricted to government-owned land, with local permit cancellations as the claimed cause.

components.statement: New data center approvals become restricted to government-owned land by 2027-11-03.
Local jurisdictions are cancelling data center permits (present-state premise).
The cancellations are the cause of the shift to government land.

dates.notes: Statement date taken from the recording's publication date.

definitions.workingDefinition: Counts as fulfilled if, by the deadline, a clear majority (say >50% by capacity or count) of newly approved data center projects in the relevant geography are sited on federal, state, or municipally owned land, or if a rule/statute formally restricts approvals to such land.
Unstated. Evaluate the United States as the most plausible scope given the Midwest examples, and record that assumption.

ambiguities: Approval vs. siting vs. construction start
supportingEvidence: Federal or state policy formally steering or restricting data center siting to public land, enacted before the deadline.
Industry siting data showing a majority of newly approved capacity on government-owned land by the deadline.
Documented pattern of local permit cancellations continuing through the window.
contradictingEvidence: Continued approvals of large private-land data center projects by local authorities through the window.
Siting statistics showing government land remains a minority of approvals.
Evidence that any shift to public land is driven by power availability or incentives rather than cancellations.
partialFulfillmentCriteria: Premise supported (cancellations documented) but future claim unsupported (approvals not restricted) → partially supported at most.
Policy announced but not enacted or implemented by the deadline → announced, not fulfilled.

outputSchemaNotes: Return evidence items with source, date, component addressed, stance, and action stage; then a two-field verdict.
researchPrompt: You are researching whether the following prediction came true. Use ONLY sources you actually retrieve through the provided search and fetch tools; never cite from memory. Proposition: within two years of 2025-11-03 (deadline 2027-11-03), approvals for new data centers became restricted to government-owned land, with local permit cancellations as the cause. Run the neutral, supporting, and disconfirming queries. For every relevant item record: URL, title, publisher, publication date, event date, a short excerpt, which component it addresses (future_claim / premise / causal_link), whether it supports, contradicts, or contextualises, and whether the action described is proposed, announced, enacted, approved, or completed. Separate events dated on or before 2027-11-03 from later developments. If searches fail or sources are inaccessible, record that as a coverage limitation — it is not evidence either way. Do not produce a verdict; return the evidence set in the required schema.
